screening_decisions.reason: Prospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI (combinations of menopausal status, ultrasound, and biomarkers) in 1218 patients with pelvic mass, using histological confirmation as reference. Meets population, intervention, and reference standard criteria.

Prospective cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study of HE4, CA125, and ROMA in 108 women with pelvic mass, referenced to final pathology. Directly evaluates test combinations in the target population.

Diagnostic accuracy study validating the IOTA ADNEX multivariable model (incorporating age, CA125, ultrasound features) in 278 women with adnexal masses, histological reference. Relevant model evaluation.

Retrospective audit of CA125 usage in 799 patients with various signs/symptoms, not a diagnostic accuracy study in a defined population of women with pelvic mass suspicious for OC. No reference standard comparison for test accuracy.

External validation study comparing ADNEX model, simple rules, LR2, and RMI variants in 326 women with adnexal masses who had surgery and pathology. Directly addresses test combinations and accuracy in the target population.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of ROMA vs RMI-I, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not provide original data meeting inclusion criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating four RMI versions (each combining menopausal status, ultrasound, and CA125) in 408 women with adnexal masses, using histopathology as reference. Fits review's focus on combinations.

Prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study comparing HE4, CA125, and ROMA in 2481 Chinese women, with discrimination between benign pelvic mass and EOC analyzed. Relevant despite inclusion of healthy controls, as main comparison targets pelvic mass population.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA in patients with benign gynaecological diseases (including ovarian cysts, myomas, endometriosis) and ovarian cancer; these conditions often present as pelvic masses. Uses histology as reference.
Systematic review summarizing symptoms associated with ovarian cancer diagnosis, not a diagnostic accuracy study of test combinations. Does not meet study design criterion.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of HE4, CA125, and ROMA; this is a synthesis of primary studies, not an original diagnostic accuracy study. Not eligible.
Global cancer statistics report (GLOBOCAN), not a diagnostic accuracy study. Irrelevant to test evaluation.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic study developing and validating the ADNEX multivariable model (combining age, CA125, ultrasound predictors) in 5909 women with ovarian masses before surgery, histology reference. Key model evaluation study.

Retrospective diagnostic accuracy study comparing CA125, HE4, ROMA, and RMI-II in 247 women with adnexal neoplasia undergoing surgery, histological reference. Evaluates test combinations relevant to review.

Prospective case-control study using 224 healthy controls and 159 women with adnexal mass; design not a cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study in a consecutive cohort of women with pelvic mass. May overestimate accuracy and does not meet primary study design criterion.

Case-control design including 140 healthy women and patients with benign cysts, endometriosis, and EOC; not a cross-sectional study in a consecutive series of women with a pelvic mass suspicious for OC. Study design introduces spectrum bias.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study comparing IOTA strategies (including LR1, LR2, simple rules with menopausal status and biomarker components) and RMI in 2403 patients with adnexal masses, histology reference. Directly addresses test combinations.

Seminal diagnostic accuracy study developing the RMI (combining CA125, ultrasound score, menopausal status) in 143 women with pelvic masses, histological confirmation. Directly relevant to the review objective.

Tissue expression study of HE4 protein by immunohistochemistry in benign and malignant tissues; not a clinical diagnostic accuracy study in women with pelvic mass. Does not evaluate test performance against a reference standard.

Diagnostic accuracy study comparing CA125, HE4, and ROMA in 373 patients with pelvic masses (malignant, benign, borderline) based on pathological confirmation. Relevant evaluation of test combinations.
Prospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125, and ROMA in 394 women with suspicious cystic ovarian masses scheduled for surgery, histological reference. Meets all inclusion criteria.

Case-control design including 106 healthy women and patients with benign gynecological diseases and ovarian cancer; not a cross-sectional study in the target population of women with a pelvic mass. Healthy controls distort spectrum.

Prospective validation of IOTA simple ultrasound rules, but compared with RMI (which incorporates menopausal status and CA125) and logistic regression models in 1938 women with adnexal masses, histological reference. Relevant as it evaluates test comparisons in the target population.

Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study evaluating ROMA (a multivariable algorithm combining CA125, HE4, and menopausal status) in postmenopausal women with ovarian mass, using histopathological confirmation as reference standard. Meets all selection criteria: population with pelvic mass, test combination of biomarkers and menopausal status, appropriate reference standard.

Not a diagnostic test accuracy study; uses age-period-cohort modeling to project cancer incidence and mortality. No evaluation of diagnostic tests or test combinations in women with pelvic mass. Does not meet selection criteria.

Qualitative study exploring women's experiences of diagnosis; not a diagnostic test accuracy study. Does not evaluate test performance or include a reference standard for ovarian cancer diagnosis. Does not meet selection criteria.

Appears to be a review or overview article on ovarian cancer biology and mouse models; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. No evaluation of test combinations, no reference standard comparison. Does not meet selection criteria.

Nested case-control study evaluating biomarker levels in prediagnostic sera from a cancer prevention trial. Population is not women with a pelvic mass suspicious for ovarian cancer; no reference standard of histological confirmation or clinical follow-up for a presenting mass. Study design does not match required cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy or trial comparing tests in the target population.

Methodological paper presenting a quality assessment tool for systematic reviews of diagnostic accuracy studies; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not evaluate any test or test combination for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Validation study of the ROMA algorithm (combines CA125, HE4, and menopausal status) using a specific assay platform in a cohort of women presenting with a pelvic mass, with histologic diagnosis as reference standard. Meets criteria for diagnostic accuracy study of a multivariable model investigating test combinations.
Narrative literature review on CA125; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not report original data on test accuracy in the target population.
Proposes a model of ovarian cancer pathogenesis based on molecular and morphological data; not a diagnostic accuracy study. Does not evaluate tests for diagnosis in women with pelvic mass.
Critical review of proteomic technologies; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. No original evaluation of test accuracy.

Observational study evaluating the risk of malignancy index (RMI; combines ultrasound, CA125, menopausal status) in women with adnexal masses, using histopathological findings as reference standard. Diagnostic accuracy study of a combination test in the target population.

Cross-sectional study assessing diagnostic accuracy of ROMA (combines HE4, CA125, menopausal status) in women with pelvic mass, using biopsy or clinical follow-up with imaging as reference standard. Evaluates test combination and provides accuracy estimates.

Retrospective analysis of preoperative test strategies including expert sonography, CA125, RMI, and their combinations in women with adnexal masses, with surgical histology as reference standard. Directly evaluates combinations of ultrasound and biomarkers along with menopausal status.

Multicenter prospective cross-sectional study evaluating the IOTA three-step ultrasound strategy (simple descriptors, simple rules, subjective assessment) in women with adnexal masses, with surgical histology as reference standard. Although focused on ultrasound, the study is a diagnostic accuracy study of a test (and potentially incorporates menopausal status implicitly through features) in the target population; included conservatively as it could inform comparisons between ultrasound and biomarker-based tests.
Methods study using simulated meta-analyses to evaluate statistical tests for publication bias; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not report test accuracy for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Cross-sectional study measuring HE4, CA125, and calculating ROMA in patients with pelvic masses (malignant, borderline, benign), using histology as reference standard. Evaluates test combinations (biomarkers and algorithm incorporating menopausal status) for ovarian cancer detection.

External validation of the ADNEX multivariable model (incorporates ultrasound features, age, serum CA125, and other clinical variables) in women with adnexal masses, using surgical histology as reference standard. Meets criteria as a study validating a multivariable model for ovarian cancer diagnosis using test combinations.

Cohort study evaluating impact of guideline implementation on referral pathways and outcomes; not a diagnostic accuracy study. Does not evaluate test performance or compare tests against a reference standard for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

Multicenter prospective study validating a predictive algorithm using HE4 and CA125, with separate models for premenopausal and postmenopausal women, in patients with pelvic mass scheduled for surgery. Reference standard is surgical histology. This is a diagnostic accuracy study of a test combination incorporating menopausal status.
Appears to be a clinical practice guideline document (likely from ACOG); not a primary diagnostic accuracy study. Does not report original test accuracy data.
Molecular genetic study investigating ARID1A mutations in ovarian cancer subtypes; not a diagnostic accuracy study. Does not evaluate tests for ovarian cancer diagnosis in women with pelvic mass.
From the fragmentary abstract, the study appears to be a narrative review or commentary on HE4 vs traditional markers; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study with a reference standard.

Prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4 and ROMA for distinguishing benign from malignant pelvic masses in Asian women, with surgical histology as reference standard. Includes evaluation of ROMA which incorporates menopausal status, CA125, HE4.

This is an epidemiological trends study using registry data; it does not evaluate any diagnostic test (ultrasound, biomarkers, or test combinations) for ovarian cancer in women with a suspicious pelvic mass, and lacks a reference standard of histology or clinical follow‑up for diagnostic accuracy.

This is a systematic review and meta‑analysis, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study (cross‑sectional or randomised trial); it does not report original test accuracy data on women with a pelvic mass.

Prospective cross‑sectional diagnostic accuracy study evaluating the ROMA index (a combination of CA125, HE4 and menopausal status) in pre‑ and postmenopausal women with adnexal masses; reference standard is surgical histopathology. Matches inclusion criteria for test combination DTA studies.

Multicentre cross‑sectional diagnostic accuracy study validating multiple multivariable models (IOTA LR2, Simple Rules, RMI) that combine ultrasound features, menopausal status and CA125 in women with adnexal masses; reference standard is surgical histology. Meets criteria for model validation DTA studies.
This is a meta‑analysis of existing studies, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study (cross‑sectional or randomised trial) in women with a suspicious pelvic mass.

Prospective cross‑sectional diagnostic accuracy study evaluating biomarkers (CA125, HE4) and composite algorithms (ROMA, RMI) that incorporate menopausal status and ultrasound; conducted in women with ovarian lesions undergoing surgery, with histopathology as reference. Fits inclusion criteria.

Multicentre diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125 and ROMA in women with suspicious pelvic mass scheduled for surgery; reference standard is histological confirmation. Meets criteria for test combination DTA studies.
Methodological article describing a statistical model for meta‑analysis; it does not present original diagnostic accuracy data from women with a pelvic mass, nor is it a primary DTA study.
Simulation study evaluating statistical methods for meta‑analysis; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study (no original patient data on ovarian cancer diagnosis in women with pelvic mass).

This is a genetic prevalence study of germline mutations in women with ovarian/fallopian tube/peritoneal carcinoma; it does not evaluate ultrasound, biomarkers or test combinations for the diagnosis of ovarian cancer in women with a pelvic mass, and lacks a diagnostic accuracy design.

Narrative review article summarising detection and treatment of ovarian cancer; not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study, and does not report original data on test accuracy in women with a suspicious pelvic mass.

Prospective multicentre blinded diagnostic accuracy study validating the ROMA algorithm (combining HE4, CA125 and menopausal status) in women presenting with an adnexal mass; reference standard is surgical pathology. Meets inclusion criteria.

Prospective diagnostic accuracy study comparing four variants of the Risk of Malignancy Index (which combine CA125, ultrasound features and menopausal status) in women with pelvic masses undergoing surgery; histological reference standard. Matches inclusion criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating Risk of Malignancy Indices (RMI 1‑4) and CA125 in postmenopausal women with adnexal masses; the RMIs incorporate ultrasound and menopausal status. Reference standard is histological diagnosis. Meets criteria despite additional inflammatory markers.

Diagnostic accuracy study assessing HE4, CA125 and the ROMA algorithm (combination of biomarkers and menopausal status) in women with benign ovarian disease and epithelial ovarian carcinoma; histological confirmation used as reference. Fits inclusion criteria.

Case‑control study identifying presenting symptoms in primary care; it does not evaluate any diagnostic test (ultrasound, biomarkers, or test combinations) for ovarian cancer, and does not report test accuracy against a reference standard of histology or clinical follow‑up in women with a pelvic mass.

Prospective validation study of the ROMA algorithm in women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery; reference standard is histopathology. Evaluates a combination of biomarkers and menopausal status. Meets inclusion criteria.

This is a systematic review and meta‑analysis of prediction models, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study. It does not contribute original test accuracy data from women with a suspicious pelvic mass.

Diagnostic accuracy study comparing single biomarkers (CA125, HE4) and combined algorithms (ROMA, RMI) that incorporate menopausal status and ultrasound in patients with ovarian masses; histological reference used. Fits inclusion criteria.

Clinical practice statement on genetic risk assessment; it is not a diagnostic test accuracy study (cross‑sectional or randomised) evaluating tests for ovarian cancer in women with a pelvic mass. No original diagnostic accuracy data reported.

Cross‑sectional diagnostic accuracy study evaluating CA125, HE4 and ROMA (combination of biomarkers and menopausal status) in Vietnamese women with ovarian masses; histopathology as reference standard. Meets inclusion criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating HE4, CA125 and ROMA (incorporates menopausal status) in postmenopausal women with ovarian tumours; histological verification used as reference. Fits inclusion criteria.

Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating 2D ultrasound, CA125, RMI (combines ultrasound, CA125, menopausal status) and IOTA models in postmenopausal women with supposed ovarian tumors; histopathology as reference standard. Meets inclusion criteria for test combination DTA studies.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not an original cross‑sectional diagnostic test accuracy study or randomised trial. Excluded because it does not provide primary data on test accuracy in the target population.

Diagnostic study enrolling 129 women with pelvic mass(es) suspicious for ovarian origin. Evaluates HE4, CA125 and the ROMA combination against histological confirmation. Matches the inclusion criteria for DTA studies of test combinations in the target population.

Prospective diagnostic accuracy study in women with complex pelvic masses. Compares HE4, CA125, ROMA and RMI against histology. Fulfills criteria for test combination evaluation with a reference standard.
This is a methodological paper describing a bias‑assessment tool, not a primary diagnostic test accuracy study or trial. No patient data or test evaluation is reported.

Cross‑sectional diagnostic study in 104 women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery. Evaluates ROMA, HE4 and CA125 using histology as reference standard. Satisfies the criteria for test combination accuracy studies.

This study categorizes routes to diagnosis using administrative data and does not evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound or biomarker tests (or combinations) in women with a pelvic mass. The design and objective are entirely different.
Methodological paper on meta‑analytic techniques. It does not contain original diagnostic test accuracy data or evaluate test combinations in the specified patient population.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic study of 901 women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery. Directly compares RMI and ROMA (which combine USS, CA125 and menopausal status) against histology. Meets the inclusion criteria for test combination DTA.
This is a software user guide and not a research study. It presents no diagnostic accuracy data and does not evaluate tests in the target population.
This is a meta‑analysis, not a primary cross‑sectional diagnostic test accuracy study or randomised trial. The review protocol requires original studies.

Uses a large multicentre database of 2445 patients with adnexal masses to evaluate the accuracy of IOTA models, simple rules and RMI, with histological confirmation as reference standard. Although retrospective, it is a cross‑sectional DTA study of test combinations and models in the required population.

Sub‑analysis of a prospective clinical trial in women undergoing surgery for an adnexal mass. Compares HE4 and CA‑125 performance for ovarian cancer, using histology as the reference standard. Fits the DTA study design and population.

This study focuses on prediction/prognosis and therapy monitoring rather than initial diagnosis. It does not clearly recruit women with a pelvic mass suspicious for ovarian cancer; patients already had a diagnosis of ovarian cancer versus controls. Excluded because it does not meet the target population or study design criteria.

The study only includes women with benign disease and reports biomarker elevation rates; it does not provide diagnostic accuracy estimates (sensitivity/specificity) for detecting ovarian cancer. Not a DTA study comparing tests with a reference standard for cancer diagnosis.
Narrative review article. Does not present original diagnostic accuracy data and is not a cross‑sectional DTA study or trial.

Reports development of a HE4 ELISA and compares post‑menopausal ovarian cancer patients with controls, but the abstract does not specify that controls were women with a pelvic mass. The target population (women with a pelvic mass suspicious for OC) is not clearly met, and the study design is not a formal DTA study with a consistent reference standard for pelvic masses.
Systematic review and meta‑analysis, not a primary DTA study or trial. The protocol requires original studies.
The condition under study is endometrial cancer, not ovarian cancer. The review’s scope is limited to ovarian cancer; studies on other cancers do not meet the population criterion.
Although it includes a validation dataset, the primary design is a meta‑analysis. The review protocol requires original cross‑sectional DTA studies; meta‑analyses are excluded.

Diagnostic study comparing CA125, HE4 and ROMA in 832 women (benign gynaecological disease and ovarian cancer). While the abstract does not explicitly state that all had a pelvic mass, a conservative interpretation suggests the benign group likely included women with adnexal masses requiring surgery; in any case, uncertainty should favour inclusion. Evaluates test combinations and uses histology/clinical diagnosis as reference.
This is a review article summarising accuracy of various diagnostic indices; it does not report original diagnostic test accuracy data from a primary study. Not a cross‑sectional DTA study or trial.

Prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study in 638 women with an unknown ovarian cyst/pelvic tumour. Compares HE4, CA125, ROMA and RMI against final pathology. Directly meets all inclusion criteria: DTA design, test combinations, reference standard, target population.

Diagnostic study in 353 women with adnexal masses (surgical patients with abnormal pelvic ultrasound) comparing the ADNEX model (which combines ultrasound findings, biomarkers, menopausal status) against histology. Evaluates a multivariable model for OC diagnosis in the required population.
